Trying to erase 1971 will be a grave mistake, says Farhad Mazhar
2025-05-01T16:44:02+06:00 | Our correspondent, Thakurgaon
https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/trying-erase-1971-will-be-grave-mistake-says-farhad-mazhar-3884791

Poet, writer, and political thinker Farhad Mazhar said last night that attempting to erase 1971 will be a grave mistake.

Speaking at a discussion event in Panchagarh last night, Farhad said, "If we attempt to erase 1971, we will be making a grave mistake. Regardless of ideology, the events of 1971 are not negotiable, they are a part of my history."

He also cautioned that Bangladesh risks descending into civil conflict if longstanding divisions over language, culture, and religion remain unresolved.

The keynote lecture, titled "The Aspiration for a New Democratic Bangladesh through Educational and Cultural Awareness: The Role of State and Society," was organised by local theatre group Bhumij at the Panchagarh Government Auditorium.

"I am a Bangla speaker. Bangla is my culture, and Islam is my religion. Just as no one can take Islam from me, no one can strip me of my language and culture," Farhad said.

"If this division is kept alive, we are bound to face civil conflict again."

"Those who made mistakes in the past must acknowledge and atone for them — they must be allowed reintegration into society," he added.

Citing the spirit of the Liberation War, Farhad argued that the 1972 Constitution no longer serves the nation's democratic aspirations and must be replaced.

"The foundational principles of equality, human dignity, and social justice should guide a new constitution," he said.

Referring to recent political shifts, Farhad described August 5 last year as a "partial victory against fascism."

He elaborated, saying, "We won a small victory, but not a full one. Because once again, we are governed under the same old fascist constitution. The Awami League remains in power, and the spectre of that constitution still looms."

He further called for the drafting of a new constitution under the principle of popular sovereignty, based on three non-negotiable clauses. Firstly, the state shall not enact any law or policy that undermines individual rights and dignity. The state shall not pass any law or policy that harms life, nature, or the environment, and the state shall not enforce any law or policy that destroys livelihoods.
